title: Omoebe with Banga Juice
author: Dobby Eghosa
desc: The four-leaf version, with the clearest leaf preparation anywhere: bitter leaf par-boiled ten minutes uncovered, the other three soaked in salt water five minutes, then all ground together.
longDesc: This is the omoebe to use if you want to understand the leaves, because it is the only source that explains how to handle them. Bitter leaf gets par-boiled for ten minutes with the lid off and then rinsed repeatedly and squeezed dry; scent leaf, uziza and ugwu are soaked in salt water for five minutes, rinsed, chopped and then ground with the washed bitter leaf and the barest amount of water. Periwinkle and fresh mackerel go in alongside the beef and pomo. There are no quantities on the page at all, and that is said plainly rather than filled in.
ingredients: Banga juice (palm fruit extract), or palm oil
steps: Par-boil the bitter leaves for 10 minutes uncovered, then rinse repeatedly with cold water and squeeze dry.
Soak the scent leaves, uziza leaves and ugwu leaves in salt water for 5 minutes.
Rinse them, chop into smaller pieces, then place in the blender with the washed bitter leaves, add minimal water, and grind.
Cook the beef and pomo with the seasoning cubes and salt for 20 minutes, until tender and the liquid reduces.
Add the smoked fish, fresh fish, banga juice, blended pepper, crayfish and periwinkles, and cook 10 minutes.
Gently pour in the blended vegetables, stir, and cook 10 to 12 minutes.
chefTips: Uncovered for the bitter leaf par-boil. The lid traps the bitterness back in; ten minutes open lets it go.
Rinse the bitter leaf repeatedly and squeeze it dry. This is the step that decides whether the finished soup is pleasantly bitter or unpleasantly so.
Five minutes in salt water for the other three leaves, no longer. It is a cleaning step, not a soak.
Minimal water in the blender. You are making a paste, and every extra spoon of water thins the finished soup.
Ten to twelve minutes for the leaves here, against two minutes in the other documented version. That is a real disagreement and it will give you a darker, softer soup.
Banga juice is palm fruit extract — the pulp, not the oil. Palm oil is offered as the alternative and it is a noticeably different dish.
This version has no quantities at all. Use the meat weights from NGA037 if you want numbers to start from.
commonMistakes: Par-boiling the bitter leaf with the lid on.
Over-soaking the tender leaves in salt water.
Flooding the blender, which waters the soup.
Substituting palm oil without expecting a different result.
sources: Adapted from 'Nigerian Black Soup recipe (Omoebe)', byline 'By Dobby', Dobby's Signature.

NO QUANTITIES ARE GIVEN FOR ANY INGREDIENT on this page. The ingredient list above is reproduced bare, exactly as printed: Fresh fish (mackerel/titus), Beef, Smoked fish, Pomo, Periwinkle, Ground crayfish, Yellow pepper ground, Banga juice (palm fruit extract) or palm oil, Scent leaves, Bitter leaves, Uziza leaves, Ugwu leaves, Seasoning cubes, Salt to taste. This is recorded as a finding rather than estimated.

THE LEAF PREPARATION, verbatim and the reason this version is published despite the absent quantities: 'Par-boil bitter leaves for 10 minutes uncovered, then rinse repeatedly with cold water and squeeze dry. Soak scent leaves, uziza leaves, and ugwu leaves in salt water for 5 minutes; rinse, chop into smaller pieces, place in blender with the washed bitter leaves, add minimal water, and grind.' No other source consulted explains how to handle the leaves at all.
Times as printed: beef and pomo 20 minutes; smoked fish, fresh fish, banga juice, pepper, crayfish and periwinkles 10 minutes; blended vegetables 10 to 12 minutes.

Her headnote, verbatim: 'Recently during one of my market runs, i stopped by mama odion's kiosk to get vegetables. She's my favorite leafy vegetable seller at the local market because she always brings the freshest vegetables daily to sell and she also gives me great discounts too.'

DISAGREEMENT on the final simmer, not reconciled: 10 to 12 minutes here against 2 minutes in the Afrolems version (NGA037). For a dish whose colour depends on oxidising the leaves, that is a material difference.

DISAGREEMENT on the leaf set: four leaves here, including uziza, against three in NGA037 which omits uziza entirely. Kitchen Butterfly's essay on the dish names five or more including ebe-ewewia and ebewewe, but carries no ingredient list, no method and no quantities at all.
CONFIRMED GAP: no leaf weights, raw or ground, in any of the four sources consulted.
reheating: Low heat. Do not boil it again.
healthBenefits: Four different leaves give an unusually broad micronutrient range.
Uziza leaf is peppery and carries piperine-family compounds.
Periwinkle is very lean and high in iron.
culturalNote: That the only source explaining how to wash the leaves is also the source with no quantities at all is a fair summary of the Nigerian written record. The knowledge that travels is the knowledge that is hard to work out for yourself; the amounts are assumed, because anyone making omoebe has seen it made.
